CONTEXT.content: Not all tasks are equal. High-risk unknowns should be tackled early via spikes — time-boxed experiments that reduce uncertainty before committing to a plan.
CONTEXT.analogy: Scouts check the bridge before the army marches across.
CONTEXT.productionNote: Projects fail when teams schedule risky work last.

DECIDE.optionA: Spike all unknowns in week 1 before any feature work.
DECIDE.optionB: Spike only when a milestone is blocked by an unknown.

tradeoffs.A: Early clarity; may delay visible progress.
tradeoffs.B: Faster start; surprises hit later when expensive.

hints: Which unknowns could kill the project if wrong?

BUILD.goal: List top 5 project risks. For the top 2, write a 2-hour spike plan with success/failure criteria.

tracks.general: Apply to your current app feature roadmap.

acceptance: 2 spike plans with time box and exit criteria
Each spike produces a go/no-go decision
hints: Spikes produce learning, not production code.
Define what you'll do if the spike fails.

criteria: Team agrees on spike priority order
hints: 'Research auth options' is not a spike without exit criteria.

BREAK.scenario: Spike reveals the chosen database can't handle required write volume. Milestone plan assumed it could.
BREAK.symptoms: Two weeks of work built on wrong assumption.
hints: What should have been spiked earlier?
How do you replan without panic?

FIX.goal: Update architecture decision and milestone plan. Add spike for the alternative before building more.
hints: Document the decision in ADR format.

decisionCallbacks.A: Week-1 spikes would have caught the database limit before building on it.
decisionCallbacks.B: Just-in-time spikes saved upfront time but cost a replan when the risk materialized.
